merged.title: Add Android support + other changes
merged.author: mateuszklysz
merged.untrustedBody:
## Added

**Game**
- Android build for arm64 (Android 10 or newer) as an SDL3 activity, in its own process and task.
- **OpenGL ES 3.2** renderer path. Shaders are still written once and translated for ES.
- **Vulkan renderer**, with a fallback to OpenGL ES when Vulkan can't start.
- **Custom Adreno drivers** (Turnip and similar) through libadrenotools.
- **On-screen pad** in the DualShock 2 style, shown only after you touch the screen.
- **In-game options drawer**, like in an emulator: graphics, sound, game options, developer tools and Quit. Opens with the options button, Back or Guide.

**Launcher**
- Runs on Android through **Tauri 2**, with the same interface as on the desktop.
- Full **controller navigation**: d-pad or stick, A, B, LB and RB. Works on the desktop too.
- Disc import with Android's file picker, including **.chd** images.
- **Game setup on the device** with a bundled Python. It keeps running in the background, with a notification.
- GPU driver packages

opened.title: fix(port): support Windows diagnostic reports and regression runs
opened.author: pezzadev
opened.untrustedBody:
On Windows, periodic `OPENRAC_REACH` reports remained at their first successful snapshot because the CRT `rename` refuses an existing destination. The gameplay regression runner also rejected built games because it searched for `openrac-<game>` without Windows' `.exe` suffix.

Use `MoveFileExA(..., MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING)` to publish completed reports on Windows, retaining the prior destination on replacement failure. Select the platform's executable filename in the regression runner. Add coverage for repeated report writes, failed replacement, missing parent directories, and Windows/Unix runner selection.

Validation:

- NTSC-U native build succeeds on Windows with Clang 19.1.1.
- Focused CTest `runtime` and `rac1-ntsc_call_abi`: 2/2 pass; zero known-target signature mismatches.
- Regression-tool unit tests: 27 pass. The new tests reproduce the respective Windows failures before the fixes.
- The normal NTSC-U New Game path reached Veldin and completed 660 scripted control ticks, ex

opened.title: feat(rac1): render Ratchet shadow volumes
opened.author: pezzadev
opened.untrustedBody:
Render Ratchet’s shadow volumes in the native PAL and NTSC ports using the retail sphere/capsule proxies posed with his animation.

Use the game’s shadow direction, ground-height clipping, distance fade and 25% darkening. Select the correct direction-table address for each version and interpolate shadows with the displayed pose.

Validation: the Windows NTSC build passes. NTSC gameplay checks sampled all 17 Blarg Station lighting zones with no shadow-direction mismatches.

PAL needs build and in-game testing. The silhouette geometry is a functional native implementation; retail pixel equivalence is not established. Shadows on other mobys are not included.

opened.title: fix(port): keep Vulkan instance buffers in the frame ring
opened.author: pezzadev
opened.untrustedBody:
Fix corrupted and disappearing Vulkan geometry by keeping instanced vertex data in the frame ring. Persistent instance buffers reproduce the failure on the AMD Radeon 780M Windows driver; per-vertex and index buffers still retain persistent storage.

Validated with the NTSC build, all 10 OpenGL/Vulkan renderer checks, 20-frame renderer replays of Veldin and Novalis, and an in-game Novalis comparison against OpenGL. Other planets and GPUs remain untested.

merged.author: xx255q

**Branch:** `cdread-gas210`. Merge this one first.

All three functions only match when their objects are assembled by the assembler retail used rather than the build's usual one. Two need **GNU as 2.10-ee-001003-1**, already in the sn-prodg-24 mirror (`toolchain/sn-prodg-24/local/sce/ee/gcc/bin/ee-as`); the third needs the DTL-S13010 build of 2.9-ee (below).

**sceCdRead** (`func_00121750`, 480 bytes, written from the assembly). 2.10-ee fills SignalSema's call slot with the volatile word load just before it.
- `config/core_text.objects` gets an optional fifth column. `gas210` (set for `00121750.o` only) makes `tools/fix_volatile_slot.py --loads` model that call-slot load; other objects keep the store-only rule. `tools/tests/test_volatile_call_slot.py` covers the rule's limits (7 tests).

**Bitstream peek** (`func_0012AAA8`, 28 bytes; the C is one shift). 2.10-ee puts the final int conversion in the return's delay slot; the old assembler gives 32 bytes. This is the function that

merged.title: Split func_001F10A0: a 36-byte remnant in front of func_001F10C8 (the debug-menu handler)
merged.author: xx255q
merged.untrustedBody:
`func_001F10A0` opens with ten instructions C cannot produce (a `daddu` and five `addiu $sp,$sp,N` runs with nops), the same dead-strip remnant shape as the earlier splits in 433afce. Its real start is `0x1F10C8`:

- `config/symbol_addrs.txt` declares `func_001F10C8`.
- `config/linker_remnants.txt` lists `text/func_001F10A0`, and `draw.c` includes it with `LINKER_REMNANT`.
- The image is unchanged.

`func_001F10C8` is 4932 bytes, the same code as `func_L00_001F4918`, the debug-menu handler shared by all 19 level programs. `nonmatching/game/func_001F10C8.c` is the level draft with the level symbols mapped to the executable's, each pair read off matching relocations (level small data sits 0x40 below the executable's). It is **BYTES 153/4932**, against the level draft's 169, and can be checked with `try_func.py` without the level dumps. A fix found there should carry over to the level copies.

Full build: 1215/1215 audited exact, every function at its retail address, the whole image match

merged.title: refactor(camera): the camera code reads its state by named fields
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
The camera system stops talking in raw offsets. All 40 camera functions (`src/game/camera.c` and the shared level copies `camera_001EB508.c`, `camera_001ED6D8.c`, `camera_001FC308.c`) now read their state through `include/camera.h`: `CameraSystem` (`gCamera`), `Camera` (the 48 slots), `CameraType`, `CameraDef`/`CameraInfo`, `CameraShake`, `CameraFollow`, `CamBlend` (lerp and orbit) and `DebugFreeCam`. Offsets are checked at compile time. The per-file aliases and private typedefs these replaced are gone.

Byte-neutral throughout: `tools/build_sn.sh` gives 1217 of 1217 exact, every function at its retail address. One rule the bytes insisted on: a sub-block reached through its own symbol keeps a pointer to it (`CamBlend *b = &gCamera.blend; b->phase = 0;` matches, `gCamera.blend.phase = 0` moves 10 bytes). One function, `Camera_ActivationCheckPriority`, keeps `state[8]`/`state[9]` raw with a comment, because the field form moved 26 bytes.

Also in here:
- `tools/file_check.py`: builds one

merged.title: Arguments retail passes in registers, NTSC ports, and the port's functional C
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
What OpenRAC's native port turned up in this decomp, sent back, plus the functional C it wrote along the way.

**Calls that drop what retail passes in registers** (a82cf741, 14f4ed57, 5a841676). Matched C that calls a function with fewer arguments than it takes, or ignores a result its callers read, still matches, because the register happens to hold the right value on the console. A port that translates the C passes 0 instead. 25 matched functions, the HUD's text width, and two more now name the arguments and results retail has. Same bytes.

**8 level functions ported from the NTSC decomp** (f4a9f722), each exact here.

**The port's functional C** (c36aeb20, 53b3dc87, 0c5f8c45, e0d3b886, 1f80d043):
- 83 functional files for functions this repo still has as assembly. 17 of them replace an older near miss's row with a corrected version that says what it fixed. The near-miss files stay where they are.
- 23 existing functional files take OpenRAC's later, checked corrections, e.g. FastVecC

Two functions, one commit each (the movie one on its own, per docs/MOVIE.md).

**setImageTag** (`func_0023C5E0`, 452 bytes): the movie code's DMA/GIF tag builder for a grid of 16x16 image blocks.
- Written from the retail assembly only; `config/movie_provenance.tsv` has its `asm only` row.
- Under `disp.c`'s `-mno-split-addresses` it stopped 39 bytes short; `disp.c` is now built without that flag. `D_0015EF84`/`D_0015EFB8` are `MACRO_ADDR`, and the display flags `D_001612E0`/`D_001612E4` go from `NOT_SDA` to `MACRO_ADDR` so `startDisplay`/`endDisplay` stay exact. All three C functions in `disp.c` are EXACT.
- That the file flag was the obstacle came out of a ChatGPT session; its C wasn't used, only the flag and declaration change, rechecked here.

**func_L14_00316E60** (880 bytes, level 14 Oltanis): starts the vendor camera, measuring its three paths and aiming it at the hero.

opened.title: Make the build and try tools run natively on Windows
opened.author: chistianh
opened.untrustedBody:
The README says Windows works natively with Git Bash (`bash tools/build.sh`), but on a plain Windows install every compile failed:

1. `cc.sh`, `build_libgcc.sh`, `build_libm.sh`, `compile_variants.sh` and `try_variants.py` always call `wine`, which does not exist on Windows (the 32-bit compilers run directly there).
2. `try_func.py` writes `Path.relative_to()` into `compile.sh`, which gives backslashes on Windows; bash reads them as escapes, so the compile never runs (it reported `COMPILE failed` for every candidate, and left stray `buildtry…log` files in the repo root).
3. `try_func.py` / `try_variants.py` fall back to `tools/docker/run.sh` when `wine` is missing, which on Windows is not needed (and usually not installed).
4. `setup_asm.sh` uses `venv/bin/python`, but on Windows the venv's interpreter is `venv/Scripts/python.exe`. `cc.sh` also runs the assembler fix-up scripts with plain `python`, which needs rabbitizer and pyelftools from the venv.

- Call the compiler t
